rationale: Escitalopram (SSRI; t½ ~27h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk) to agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist, 5-HT2C antagonist; t½ ~2h; no serotonergic reuptake activity). Switch reasons: sexual dysfunction, weight gain, inadequate response on SSRI, desire for sleep-targeting antidepressant. Escitalopram has moderate discontinuation syndrome risk — taper gradually over at least 2 weeks. Agomelatine can be started during the escitalopram taper without serotonin syndrome risk (agomelatine does not inhibit serotonin reuptake). CRITICAL: LFTs must be checked BEFORE starting agomelatine (hepatotoxicity monitoring baseline). Agomelatine is contraindicated in hepatic impairment. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Continue escitalopram 20 mg. CHECK BASELINE LFTs (ALT) BEFORE starting agomelatine — mandatory hepatotoxicity monitoring. If ALT >3× ULN do not start agomelatine. No serotonin overlap concern — agomelatine has no serotonergic reuptake activity.
Reduce escitalopram to 10 mg. Continue agomelatine 25 mg. Monitor for discontinuation symptoms (dizziness, 'brain zaps', mood change) — mild at this step.

Stop escitalopram. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Some patients may experience brief discontinuation symptoms on final escitalopram stop — usually mild and self-limiting with escitalopram. Titrate agomelatine to 50 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Escitalopram 20 mg → agomelatine 25 mg (standard doses for MDD). Not pharmacologically equivalent — different mechanisms. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: Hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or above) — agomelatine contraindicated.
ALT >3× ULN at baseline — do not start agomelatine.
